IF YOU WANT TO CRACK CODING INTERVIEWS, STOP PRACTICING RANDOMLY.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 PATTERNS INSTEAD:

Two pointers turn O(n^2) into O(n).

Sorted array, pair sum, container with water. Move ends inward instead of nesting loops.

Sliding window owns substring problems.

Longest, shortest, best. Grow the right edge, shrink the left when invalid. One pass.

BFS and DFS are the same skill.

Grids, islands, trees, graphs. Queue for shortest path, stack for exhaustive search. Learn both once.

IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A TOP 1% PROBLEM SOLVER, STOP SKIPPING THE BASICS.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 HABITS:

Always clarify before coding.

Inputs, edge cases, constraints. Five minutes of questions saves thirty minutes of rewrites.

Brute force first, on purpose.

Write the ugly O(n^2), then ask what repeats. The optimal solution hides inside the naive one.

Time yourself, then review.

45 minutes per problem max. The learning happens in the 15 minutes after, studying the pattern you missed.

IF YOU WANT TO MASTER DYNAMIC PROGRAMMING, STOP FEARING IT.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 STEPS:

Ask one question: does the answer build from smaller answers?

If yes, it's DP. If no, stop forcing it.

Define the state in one sentence.

dp[i] means the best answer for the first i items. Vague state, wrong answer.

Write the recurrence before any code.

How does dp[i] use dp[i-1]? One line of math beats fifty lines of guessing.
